newsitem.title: CHINA: China says movie, pop stars spoiled by adulation.
newsitem.headline: China says movie, pop stars spoiled by adulation.

text.p: China slammed movie stars and pop singers on Monday , saying they have been spoiled by adulation heaped on them by fans and the media.
"The thinking of some famous stars has undergone a change and the stink of money has become their god," the official Legal Daily lamented.
The newspaper urged actors and singers to abandon the reckless pursuit of fortune and fame and learn to serve their audiences above all else.
Almost two decades of economic reforms have eroded communist puritanism and set the people free to make money. Paramount leader Deng Xiaoping coined the slogan "To get rich is glorious".
The ranks of China's movie and pop stars have swollen with rapid economic growth and are increasingly sought for lucrative promotional gigs and television talk shows.
The newspaper singled out one actor who specialised in playing an unidentified revolutionary communist leader, but demanded a high fee for appearing in benefit performances in poor regions.
"How can a singer who knows only money and has no concern for the audience be able to pour all his body and heart and aesthetic feeling into singing?" the newspaper asked.
Last month, China's propaganda tsars launched a drive to promote socialist ethics to counter what they say are harmful capitalist and Western influences on the moral fabric of society.
